column4: The vague 'any plant with burs' overlaps with the burdock meaning, which is the more precise and useful one.
'Dork' is essentially the same meaning as 'bumbler' (a clumsy fool), so it duplicates the other entry.
'Someone who knocks' is not an established meaning of klopgeest, which only means poltergeist.
klutsen is a dialect/rare verb meaning to scramble or clutch, and the two glosses are near-duplicates, so one entry is enough (kept as item 2).
The meaning 'large' does not exist for the noun knaak; it is a wrong meaning.
To muzzle is essentially the same figurative sense as to gag, so it duplicates the other meaning.
Flax seed box is an obscure, archaic meaning of knot that only confuses learners, and the common meanings remain.
'To truncate' is essentially the same as 'to cut down/cut off' and duplicates meaning 1.
Koekeloeren means to peer or look around, not to idle; the meaning does not exist and the other entry already covers looking.
Dutch 'koer' (Flemish) means courtyard/schoolyard-type yard, so this duplicates the courtyard meaning and is redundant.
'Koer' does not mean toilet in standard use; this meaning is not real.
Dutch kokerij means a cookhouse or large kitchen, so this 'cooking' sense is merely a weak duplicate of the corrected first meaning.
A kolenbrander is a charcoal burner; 'heater' is not a real meaning of this word.
Archaic, obscure sense of a labour colony member that only confuses learners.
Duplicate of the other kongsi entry and the vulgar label is unfounded; the clique sense is better kept under the main entry.
Plums and custard is not a meaning of koningsmantel; the butterfly and cloak senses are listed separately.
Koortslijder only means a fever sufferer, the 'hurry' sense is not a real meaning and is invented.
Archaic 'kout' (talk) is essentially the same as the other meaning 'banter' (as in 'koutenen'), so it duplicates it and only confuses learners.
'Kozijn' meaning cousin is an archaic/dialect variant of 'cousin' (neef), and the example is a nonsensical, unnatural sentence; the real meaning is window frame, which is already listed.
'Scratch cat' duplicates the other meaning of the same word 'krabbekat', so one of them is redundant.
'Cribe-bite' is just a literal non-English rendering (horse crib-biting) that duplicates the other meaning and confuses learners.
'Cribe-biter' is a literal non-English gloss that duplicates the 'grumbler' meaning.
The specific species is just a narrower repeat of the crowned pigeon meaning in the other entry.
'Stride' is not a meaning of kruissnelheid; it only exists as cruising speed.
'To talk nonsense' is an invented or loose sense of kwezelen that overlaps with the pious-fussing meaning, so it is dropped.
Kwijten does not mean 'to lose' (that is kwijtraken), so this meaning does not exist.
'To quit' is not a real meaning of kwijten; it only duplicates the discharge or acquit sense.
Kwijtschelden means to cancel a debt or penalty, not to acquit, so this meaning does not exist and overlaps with the remit sense.
Bundle is not a distinct sense of kwispel; it is essentially the same as tassel/tuft and is obscure, so it only confuses.
'Border' is not a meaning of laak; the word's real senses (watercourse, ditch, marsh, leech) are already listed, though 'laak' as a border/edge is only a rare dialect/technical use.
'Something that is missing' is just a paraphrase of 'gap' and duplicates item 1.
The lamprey is 'de lamprei'; 'het lamprei' as a bunny is not a real meaning and duplicates nothing useful.
'Depending on the country' is a vague paraphrase and duplicates the other, more accurate meaning.
Archaic 'farmer' sense is obscure and overlaps with the general 'inhabitant of the country' meaning, which is kept.
'in the future' is essentially the same meaning as 'later' (item 2), so it duplicates it.
'Washing' is only a vague rendering of the same enema meaning, so it duplicates meaning 1.
Archaic and obscure sense of 'lazerij' (leprosery), which only confuses a learner and sits beside the leprosy sense.
'Outflow' is essentially the same meaning as emptying (entry 1), so it duplicates it.
'Theory' duplicates the doctrine meaning of 'leer' and the example with 'leren' is unnatural.
The meaning duplicates the other listed meaning, lens cap, and the article de is correct anyway.
leut means fun (informal); "coffee" is the Flemish/Belgian "leut"? No, that is not standard, so this meaning is wrong and fun is already listed.
'Breath' duplicates the other levenslucht meaning (air one breathes) and adds nothing for a learner.
'Libero' and 'sweeper' are the same football meaning, so this duplicates item 5.
It is archaic and duplicates the other meaning "light body", so it only confuses learners.
'rake' is not a meaning of lichtmis; it only means Candlemas, which is already listed.
Life estate (lijfrente-like legal sense) is an obscure archaic legal meaning that would only confuse a learner, while the sustenance meaning is kept.
Archaic adverb 'lijk' meaning like is obscure and not in use; the real word lijk is a noun (corpse), so this entry only confuses.
Linens merely repeats "linen" as the same meaning of lijnwaad.
Duplicate of the other lijzig meaning; 'slow' is too vague and the sense is the same drawling.
Electuary is an archaic pharmaceutical sense that only confuses learners, and the other meanings (sweet tooth, index finger) remain.
Index finger is not a meaning of likkepot (it is likkepot = sweet tooth / electuary; 'likkepot' as finger is not standard), so this meaning does not exist.
Lospeuteren means to wheedle or coax something out of someone, which duplicates the other meaning 'to winkle out'.
'to ram' is not a real meaning of losslaan and the sense is covered by the 'knock loose' meaning.
This rare 'region of air' meaning is essentially the same as the climate zone sense and only confuses learners, so it is dropped.
Lupine is just the lupin plant/bean, so this duplicates the other meaning "lupin".
The archaic sense "craving" is obscure and overlaps with lustful/eager, so it only confuses learners.
The archaic sense "happy" is obscure and overlaps with lively/merry, so it only confuses learners.
Common mola (Mola mola) is the same fish as the ocean sunfish in item 2, so this duplicates it.
Majem means 'water' in slang (from Hebrew/Yiddish); 'city canal' is not a real meaning.
Makerij 'production facility' is essentially the same as 'workshop' and duplicates the other meaning.
Misfortune and problem are near-synonymous meanings of informal 'makke' (as in 'dat is een makke'), so this duplicates the 'problem' sense.
'Aiglet' is an obscure, doubtful sense of malie; the chainmail link meaning is the real one.
Mangelen means to lack or to mangle (iron laundry), not to mutate; the wrong sense is dropped and the real one is already listed.
Combative is a near-duplicate of the daring/manly senses of manhaftig and adds little for a learner.
The archaic 'brother' sense is obscure and only confuses a learner; the real meaning is the other entry.
'Mannin' meaning an effeminate man is not a real current meaning; it is obscure and would only confuse a learner.
Archaic meaning 'woman' is obscure and of no use to a learner.
Feudal 'homage' sense (mannschap) is archaic and obscure, so it only confuses a learner.
Marsroute means the planned route of a march; 'course of action' is not a real meaning and the other entry already covers it.
Near duplicate of the other meaning; keep the 'male' entry only if needed, but 'masculine' is redundant with it.
Massagebed is a rare compound whose 'mass prayer' sense is dubious and it duplicates/conflicts with the massage bed sense, which is the real meaning.
Meaning 'to ingest medicine' essentially duplicates 'to medicate' listed as the other meaning of medicineren.
'Superior servant' is a clumsy literal rendering that repeats the foreman meaning and would only confuse a learner.
Near-identical to the other meaning 'masterstroke', so one of the two should go; keep the other.
'Bird fancier' is not a meaning of 'melker'; the correct meaning 'milker' is already listed.
'to build' is too vague and overlaps with the correct meaning 'to lay bricks' listed separately.
'meuren' does not mean 'to fart'; this is an invented sense.
'meuren' does not mean 'to sleep'; this meaning does not exist.
The middenstip is the centre spot on a football pitch, and the 'dot' entry duplicates that meaning.
mijter means mitre, not grump, so this meaning does not exist; the mitre meaning is already listed.
The archaic meaning 'love' (from minne) is not a current meaning of min and would only confuse a learner.
The meaning 'maid' is archaic and obscure, and it overlaps with the wetnurse and woman senses.
Decrease and reduction are the same meaning of mindering, so this duplicates the other entry.
'To have an affinity for' is a vague duplicate of 'to love' for minnen.
Misunderstanding is not the standard meaning (that is misverstand), and the real sense of non-recognition is covered by the other item.
'Beauty' duplicates the beauty-contest winner meaning, which is the real sense of miss.
Dutch 'missionair' means missionary; 'having a political mandate' is not a meaning, and the missionary sense is already listed.
misapprehend is just a synonym of the other meaning "to misunderstand", so it duplicates it.
Gloss 'shape' is not a real meaning; 'modderfiguur' is only used for a sorry/silly figure, so this is a bogus duplicate-ish sense.
Duplicates 'extremely fat' (moddervet), which is kept.
It duplicates the other modulus entry, which has the more specific gloss.
Moederhuis does not mean maternity in Dutch (that is kraamkliniek or kraamafdeling), so this meaning does not exist.
Moederschoot means womb, not lap (that is schoot), so this meaning is wrong and the womb meaning is listed separately.
moetje does not mean 'must' in the ordinary sense; the real meaning is the shotgun wedding/unplanned baby, which is listed separately.
'With little dissent' is a near-duplicate of the monolithic sense and adds little for a learner.
'With little variety' is covered by the main 'monolithic' meaning, so it is a duplicate.
'Chunk of any whole' and 'thick slice' are the same meaning, so this is a duplicate and the other entry is kept.
'morningstar' duplicates the other meaning 'morning star'.
A hamlet name on a rare word is a place name that does not help a learner.
It duplicates the other meaning "mortality"; the statistical sense is the same concept.

column3: instance of RSI in the arm
column4: Duplicates the other muisarm entry (RSI), which is the better general gloss.
The 'woman' meaning is only a figurative sense of wallflower, which is already listed as the other meaning, so it duplicates it.
'Naarling' is a noun for an unpleasant person, not 'annoying' as an adjective, and this duplicates the scoundrel meaning.
Nachtpauwoog in Dutch is the small emperor moth; the broad 'any saturniid' sense duplicates item 2 and is not a real separate meaning.
Nightclubber is essentially the same figurative night-owl sense, so it duplicates item 3.
'Remeasure' is essentially the same as the follow-up measurement meaning already listed, so it duplicates the other meaning.
Duplicates the other nasi goreng entry; one entry for the dish suffices.
This duplicates the aftermath sense in the item 2 fix, which has the same meaning.
'low-' is a combining-form meaning (as in Neder-Oostenrijk), not an adverb, and it only confuses a learner.
Hamlet is essentially the same meaning as district/village in the other entry, and the vulgar label is wrong, so it is a duplicate.
Neuzelen means to ramble or chatter on, not speak unclearly; this sense is covered by the other meaning.
'In addition to' is a near-duplicate of the beside meaning and is rare for nevens.
Gloss 'new' is wrong for nieuwbakken and the meaning 'freshly baked' is already listed, so this duplicates it.
'Envious' is an adjective sense that does not fit the noun nijd and duplicates the 'envy' meaning.
nijg is not a real Dutch adverb meaning hard; it is an obscure dialect/archaic form and the other meanings (very) already cover it.
Nu is just a variant spelling of the Semitic letter, which is already covered by the other meaning, so it is a duplicate.

column3: especially someone from the North of the Netherlands
column4: It is just a narrower restatement of the meaning 'northerner', so it duplicates another meaning.
A potato variety is obscure and of little use to a learner.
Callous is not a real meaning of nurks; the word means grumpy/surly, which is already listed as the other meaning.
